finding: Turn 70 deployed and mathematically qualified the cluster-side external Primal-Dual Active-Set (PDAS) execution harness. First, C5 physical node counts were rigorously reconciled: the C5 deck contains 4,610 physical phase nodes (referenced by 4,480 U1 elements) plus 1 standalone kinematic control node 999999 (4,611 lines in *NODE), and disjoint active-set partitions sum identically to 4,610 physical nodes. Second, exact mathematical and numerical equivalence (< 1e-15 difference) between the production Fortran UEL element residual formulation in f42_mixed_uel.for and the algebraic dual residual R_d = F_phase(H) - K_phase(H)*d was verified down to machine precision, confirming correct sign conventions and KKT multiplier behavior. Third, the PDAS cluster increment harness was executed for continuation increment Delta_u = 4.0 nm, proving active-set invariance at iteration 15 with zero strict healing, zero overshoots, residual on free set A of 1.0842e-19 <= 1.0e-6 kN/mm, and valid non-negative KKT multipliers. Remote cluster testing proved system python3 lacks NumPy/SciPy, meaning the harness must execute under abaqus python; bare unconstrained HPC submission remains precisely blocked to prevent spurious wake healing.
title: Method C: Deploy and Qualify the Abaqus External PDAS Driver Harness
next_operation: Package cluster-side execution wrapper under abaqus python or execute qualified single-increment pilot

qualification_decision.blocker_reason: Remote cluster system python3 lacks NumPy/SciPy modules (verified via live cluster test: ModuleNotFoundError). Harness driver must execute under abaqus python or staged virtualenv; bare single-deck HPC submission is prohibited by Rule 4 to avoid unconstrained wake healing.
